newsitem.title: UK: British Steel extends gains on weaker pound.
newsitem.headline: British Steel extends gains on weaker pound.

text.p: Shares in British Steel Plc climbed on Wednesday for a third consecutive day as weaker sterling continued to buoy companies with major overseas earnings, dealers said.
British Steel shares gained 5p, or three percent, to 170p by 0743 GMT, making it the second biggest gainer in the FTSE 100 index.
Dealers also noted British Steel ADRs rose $1-11/16 to $28-1/4 in New York on Tuesday where HSBC James Capel crossed 250,000 ADRs, the equivalent of 2.5 million shares, at $28.00.

Overseas earners in the engineering sector such as GKN Plc also benefited from the recent dip in sterling strength and its shares gained 20p to 1077-1/2p. Likewise, TI Group Plc advanced 8-1/2p to 555p and Smiths Industries Plc jumped 17p to 802p.
On the foreign exchanges on Wednesday, the sterling/mark rate was quoted at 2.9980 by 0816 GMT, down from its year high of 3.0878 reached on July 23.
